diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exist a compact set $\mathcal{K}\subset \mathbb{C}^d$, with $\mathcal{U} \subset \mathcal{K}$,

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem requires both U ⊂ K (via the Assumption) and K ⊂ U. Hence K = U = [-1,1]^d ⊂ R^d, whose interior in C^d is empty. The asserted holomorphic extension to the interior of K is then vacuous, and no compact H inside that interior is nonempty. The corollaries assume a polyellipse inside the interior of K, which cannot hold under the theorem's stated hypothesis. The proof actually uses U ⊂ K with a nonempty interior.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by U ⊂ K, which is the inclusion already given in the Assumption and used in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the holomorphy theorem is empty, and the corollaries cannot invoke it under their polyellipse hypotheses.
issues.title: Main theorem hypothesis K ⊂ U makes the theorem vacuous and incompatible with its uses
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol local correction consistent with the Assumption and the proof restores the theorem and all its uses, with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: From ∂_t v ≤ 2 r(M̃) v and r ≤ β, one obtains only ∂_t v ≤ 2β v; the displayed ∂_t v ≤ β v does not follow. The derivation has three further gaps. (1) The Gronwall conclusion exp(2∫β) is inconsistent with the inequality just written. (2) ṽ is a supremum over z whose differentiability is never established, so ṽ' ≤ βṽ is unjustified. (3) ṽ bounds the squared norm, whereas eq:unif_upper_bound_ext bounds the norm, so 'corresponds' conflates the two. The stated bound B does survive: applying Gronwall for each fixed z gives ||ũ(T,z)||_2 ≤ ||u_0|| exp(∫β) ≤ B.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each fixed z, apply Gronwall to ∂_t v ≤ 2β(t) v to get v(T,z) ≤ ||u_0||^2 exp(2∫β). Take square roots and then the supremum over H to obtain a bound that is at most B.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of eq:unif_upper_bound_ext is invalid as written. The bound itself, and hence its uses in the corollaries, remains true.
issues.title: Invalid steps in the Gronwall derivation of the uniform bound
issues.why_classification: A short routine rewrite of the Gronwall step yields an even stronger bound, and all statements are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The LS estimator is linear in the data. Take n = 0 and replace f by αf, which is still holomorphic on the same polyellipse. Then f̂ becomes αf̂ and the error scales by |α|, while the right-hand side C(ρ,p)(m/log(m/ε))^{1/2-1/p} is fixed. For any f outside the finite span of {ψ_ν : ν ∈ S}, the error is positive, so the bound fails as |α| → ∞. The same holds in cor:LS: f_v is linear in u_0, but the constant does not depend on u_0. This contrasts with the CS results, which carry ||f||_{L^∞(E_ρ)} or B. The exponent p is also left unquantified.

failure_location.quote: for any $f: \mathcal{U} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ that admits a holomorphic extension to a Bernstein polyellipse $\mathcal{E}_{\bm{\rho}} \subset \mathbb{C}^d$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State th:main_ls for f with ||f||_{L^∞(E_ρ)} ≤ 1, or multiply the bound by ||f||_{L^∞(E_ρ)}, and specify the range of p. In cor:LS, insert the factor B(u_0,T,M) using Step 2 of thm:mainthm with H = E_ρ.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-dimensional LS theorem and the headline LS convergence corollary are false as stated.
issues.title: LS error bound lacks the ||f||_{L^∞(E_ρ)} (or B) factor and is false by scaling
issues.why_classification: Both the supporting theorem and the main LS corollary must be restated with a data-dependent constant, and the corollary must newly invoke the bound B. The rate and the method survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, there exists a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}_0^d$ of cardinality $|S| \leq \lceil m/\log(m/\epsilon) \rceil$ such that the following holds with probability at least $1 - \epsilon$ for any $f: \mathcal{U} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$
For this reason, the best $s$-term approximation support $S$ can be chosen in $\mathbb{N}_0^d \times \{0\}^\mathbb{N}$.
$\varrho$ be either the uniform or Chebyschev measure on $\mathcal{U}=[-1,1]^d$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts one set S, chosen before f, that works for every f holomorphic on E_ρ. The proof instead reasons about 'the support of the best s-term approximation to f', which depends on f. It never shows that d-variate polyellipse-holomorphic functions satisfy the hypotheses of the cited infinite-dimensional result. Nor does it show that the f-independent set produced there lies in N_0^d × {0}^N. In addition, the vanishing computation integrates against Lebesgue dx. In the Chebyshev case this is false: ∫_{-1}^{1} T_2(x) dx = -2/3 ≠ 0.

failure_location.quote: We only need to prove that the support $S$ of the best $s$-term approximation to $f$ satisfies $S \subset \mathbb{N}_0^d \times \{0\}^\mathbb{N}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Show that every f holomorphic on a neighborhood of E_ρ, viewed as a function independent of x_j for j > d, belongs to the class handled by the cited theorem. The class parameters should depend only on ρ and be trivial in coordinates j > d, so that the cited f-independent set lies in N_0^d × {0}^N. Write all integrals with respect to ϱ.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of a uniform f-independent set S in th:main_ls, and hence cor:LS, is unsupported.
issues.title: Proof of the finite-dimensional LS theorem does not establish an f-independent set S
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial reduction argument is needed. Once it is supplied, the stated LS guarantee and rate survive unchanged.
